about: Four invented questions about a bakery's ordering page; the first two are already answered.

questions.title: How should an order be confirmed?
questions.why: Customers ask whether the order went through. The answer decides what we build first.
facts: Most orders come in between 6 and 8 in the morning.
Text messages cost a small amount per order.

options.label: Email only
options.detail: Free, but some people never open it before pickup.

options.label: Email and a text
options.detail: The text arrives within a minute.

options.label: On the screen only
options.detail: Nothing to send, and nothing to look back at.

questions.reason: The text is what people check at 7 am, and the cost is small next to a missed pickup.

questions.title: How long is a pickup window?
questions.why: Shorter windows spread the queue but make the day's grid longer to fill.
facts: The counter handles about 12 pickups an hour.

options.label: 30 minutes
options.detail: Six slots over the busy morning.

options.label: 15 minutes
options.detail: Twelve slots over the busy morning.

questions.reason: It matches the counter's real pace.

questions.title: What does a sold-out loaf look like?
questions.why: A hidden loaf leaves people wondering; a visible one invites a second choice.
facts: Rye and seeded sell out most Saturdays.
A waiting list needs a way to tell people when more is baked.

options.label: Show it as sold out
options.detail: Greyed, with the next bake day.

questions.reason: It is the least work and keeps the menu honest.

questions.title: Who may change the weekly menu?
questions.why: Edits go live at once, so a wrong price shows up for every customer.

options.label: Any staff member
options.detail: With the owner told after each change.

questions.reason: Two people have asked to help; they can ask the owner for now.

slots.label: 30 minutes
slots.note: Start with 30 and look at the first month.
slots.claude: Built with 30 minute windows; the length is one setting, so changing it later is a one-line edit.

log.what: applied it to the order page
